corrections.originalCritique: Strongest feature: The reply directly defeats the dilemma's claimed exhaustiveness by presenting a third relation in which commands express God's necessary character, thereby avoiding both an external moral standard and unconstrained voluntarism. Principal limitation: Identifying God with the good may label rather than explain objective goodness unless the account supplies substantive content, constraints on divine character, and a bridge from that character to particular obligations. Live burden: Edwards must clarify why divine nature is independently recognizable as good and how it generates authoritative duties, while Woodford must engage this necessary-nature theory rather than continue targeting simple command voluntarism.
